gap._description: Zig declaration surface modeled from the pinched tree-sitter-zig AST (probe-verified 2026-08-29 against the upstream Zig compiler corpus, 2,950 .zig files). opaque_declaration and test_declaration parse cleanly but are NOT emitted as standalone symbols: opaque types have no members to surface (Zig models interfaces via vtables, not class inheritance), and `test` blocks are anonymous scoped bodies without a stable callable name. Their internal call/use edges ARE captured (source '(global)'). differential zig:zig is 0 missing / 0 unexplained at the pinned floor. No analyzer literal references a non-existent grammar node type (dead literals boolean_literal/char_literal/number_literal/type_identifier removed in the zig wave).

gaps.missing: `opaque {}` types parse cleanly but emit no symbol. Zig models runtime interfaces via opaque types + function pointers (no class inheritance), so there are no fields/extends to surface; the type is intentionally not indexed.

`test "name" {}` blocks emit no function symbol (anonymous, unstable scope). Calls and field-uses inside a test body are still captured with source '(global)', so the code-intel graph does not lose them.

decisions.question: Zig has no class inheritance, no interfaces with implements clauses, no overrides, and no implicit type instantiation the way C++/Java do — how are these relationship kinds handled?
decisions.resolution: By design, Zig emits NO extends/implements/overrides/instantiates edges. Composition is expressed through struct fields and opaque vtables; generics are compile-time monomorphized without a runtime type dispatch the analyzer can attribute statically. requiredKinds for zig reflect only the emitted kinds: calls, uses, contains, references.

decisions.question: Zig evaluates top-level `const`, `comptime`, and `test` block initializers at compile time — these are call sites outside any function body.
decisions.resolution: Field-accesses and calls in any non-function context (top-level const initializers, comptime blocks, test bodies) emit with source '(global)', mirroring the go family package-scope-call contract. Without this, fmt.zig's `const assert = std.debug.assert;` (a real dependency) would be silently dropped — measured 745 edges were lost before this fix (zig wave 2026-08-29).

decisions.question: Error-set members (`error{ A, B }`) are identifiers, and @-prefixed builtins are intrinsics, not user symbols.
decisions.resolution: An identifier whose parent is error_set_declaration is emitted as an EnumMember (members cannot collide with the declaring variable's LHS). @builtin_function callees (@import/@intCast/@as) are compile-time intrinsics and emit NO calls edge — they are never user symbols.
